defects.description: formatPercentLegacy() is exported but referenced nowhere: not in src/, not in tests/, not re-exported from src/index.ts. It was the table's percent formatter until the valuation/peg commit switched the table to formatPct().
defects.detection_hint: Reference search for formatPercentLegacy finds only its definition; package.json "exports" exposes only "." (dist/index.js), so a deep import is impossible and the export is not public API.

defects.description: The whole module (holdingsToCsv) is unused. Its only importer was the old --csv flag of the value command, removed by the 'refactor(cli): rename check to alerts' commit; the file was left behind.
defects.detection_hint: No file imports util/csv(.js); not re-exported from src/index.ts; git log -S holdingsToCsv shows the CLI usage being deleted.

defects.description: Runtime dependency "dotenv" is declared (and locked in pnpm-lock.yaml) but never imported; nothing loads a .env file. .env.example only documents variables that are read from process.env directly.
defects.detection_hint: grep for 'dotenv' in src/ and tests/ finds nothing; knip / depcheck report it as unused. Fix = remove from package.json and refresh pnpm-lock.yaml.

defects.description: Commented-out private dedupe() method left in AlertEngine after cooldowns moved to per-rule-id state. Version control already keeps it.
defects.detection_hint: Block of '//'-prefixed TypeScript statements inside the class body.

defects.description: normalizeAssetName() duplicates normalizeAsset() from src/exchange/symbols.ts (lines 12-16) but never received the 'fix(symbols): resolve kraken asset aliases and trim whitespace' fix. Config holdings/rules/pegged written as "xbt" or "BTC " stay "XBT" / "BTC ", so the wrong symbol is requested (no ticker) and the holding is silently valued at 0 (see D09) or the rule never fires.
defects.detection_hint: Two asset-normalization functions; the one in symbols.ts trims and resolves ASSET_ALIASES, the config copy only upper-cases. Fix = call normalizeAsset() from the config loader and delete the copy.

defects.description: parseArgs() is a ~110-line hand-rolled parser with nesting depth 6, a 13-way '||' option list and ~40 decision points (flags, inline '=' values, numeric validation, per-command option checks) in one function. Node 24 ships util.parseArgs.
defects.detection_hint: Cyclomatic/cognitive complexity far above any threshold (>30); deepest nesting in the repo. Any refactor must preserve the exact accepted syntax and error messages (the hidden CLI tests pin them).

defects.description: dispatch() catches every notifier failure without binding the error and logs it at debug level (below the default 'info'), so a broken webhook or unwritable alert file is invisible. check() still records the cooldown for the rule (line 86) even when every notifier failed, so the alert is lost for the whole cooldown window.
defects.detection_hint: 'catch {' with only a log.debug call and no error in the log fields; delivered count is not used to decide whether to record lastFired.

defects.description: Any failure to read or parse the config (missing file, typo in --config, malformed JSON) is downgraded to a warn log and DEFAULT_CONFIG is returned. `pricewatch value --config nope.json` prints a 0.00 USDT portfolio and exits 0; `alerts` runs with no rules. It also returns the shared mutable DEFAULT_CONFIG object.
defects.detection_hint: catch-all around readFile + JSON.parse that returns a default value; run the built CLI with a non-existent config path and observe exit code 0.

defects.description: A non-pegged asset with no ticker (unknown symbol, delisting, HTTP error, rate limit) is priced at 0 with priceSource 'exchange'. Totals, PnL and the drawdown rule are silently wrong; only a warn line from getTickers hints at it. The fix belongs here (throw, or mark the holding as unpriced and surface it), not in getTickers, whose skip-on-failure is the documented ExchangeClient contract the peg fallback relies on (trap X05/X08).
defects.detection_hint: Final 'return { price: 0, source: "exchange" }' after the ticker and peg lookups; the returned source even claims the price came from the exchange.

defects.description: FetchHttpClient calls fetch() with no AbortSignal/timeout. A stalled exchange or webhook connection hangs `alerts` (cron) and `watch` indefinitely; the limiter and sequential loop mean one hung request blocks every later asset.
defects.detection_hint: fetch(url, { method, headers, body }) without 'signal'; no timeout option on FetchHttpClient.

defects.description: Positions and cost basis are accumulated in binary floating point and compared exactly. Buy 0.1 + buy 0.2 then sell 0.3 leaves qty 5.55e-17, so a closed position is reported as an open holding with a meaningless avgCost; buy 0.3 then sell 0.1 and sell 0.2 throws 'sell of 0.2 BTC exceeds open position of 0.19999999999999998'. Money totals elsewhere (valuation, snapshot round()) use the same float arithmetic.
defects.detection_hint: 'pos.qty === 0' and 't.quantity > pos.qty' on values built with += / -= of decimal fractions; no decimal/integer-unit representation or tolerance.

defects.description: orderId is converted with Number() (and typed number in src/types.ts line 8). Exchange order ids above 2^53 (18-19 digit ids such as "653718423119753216" and "653718423119753217") round to the same double, so dedupeTrades() treats two different orders as duplicates and drops a real fill, corrupting positions and PnL.
defects.detection_hint: Number(raw.orderId) on an id that arrives as a string; Number.isSafeInteger is never checked. Fix = keep ids as strings (public Trade type change).

defects.description: this.state.save(lastFired) is not awaited ('fire-and-forget'). check() resolves before cooldowns are persisted, and a write failure (EACCES, disk full) becomes an unhandled rejection that crashes the process after the summary was already printed, with no context.
defects.detection_hint: Promise-returning call used as a statement; typescript-eslint no-floating-promises (enabled in eslint.config.mjs) flags it.

defects.description: A bare '// @ts-ignore' (no reason) hides TS2769: body.result may be undefined. A payload without 'result' or with an empty result throws a raw TypeError instead of an ExchangeError; the response is also blindly cast at line 41 (res.body as KrakenTickerResponse).
defects.detection_hint: Removing the comment makes `tsc --noEmit` fail at kraken.ts:47; eslint ban-ts-comment (configured) rejects @ts-ignore.

defects.description: File-wide '/* eslint-disable */' with no rule list or reason, added by the 'chore: add eslint flat config' commit to silence the typed rules on the `raw: any` validators (lines 38-112). It disables every rule, including no-floating-promises and the unsafe-any family, for the module that parses untrusted input.
defects.detection_hint: Blanket disable on line 1; the file is the only one using 'any'. Fix = type the input as unknown and narrow, or at least scope the disable to named rules with a justification.

defects.description: The ticker cache (line 89) is keyed by `${base}/${quote}@${timeBucket}` and entries are never evicted. In `watch` mode every interval creates new keys, so memory grows without bound for the life of the process (one entry per asset per check: 1,440 per asset per day at the default 60 s watch interval).
defects.detection_hint: Map with set() but no delete()/size cap; key includes Math.floor(now / ttl).

defects.description: dedupeTrades() uses filter + findIndex, O(n^2): a 50k-row export costs ~1.25e9 comparisons. A Set/Map of seen ids gives the same first-occurrence, order-preserving result in O(n).
defects.detection_hint: findIndex inside filter over the same array.

defects.description: Comment narrates the editing session ('Changed this session ... as the user asked') instead of explaining the code; meaningless to future readers.
defects.detection_hint: References to 'this session' and 'the user asked' in a source comment.

defects.description: 'Step 1' ... 'Step 5' comments restate each following line ('now we calculate the value...'); pure noise typical of generated code.
defects.detection_hint: Numbered step comments that paraphrase the next statement.

defects.description: README documents a `check` command (commands table and the cron example) that was renamed to `alerts`; following the README gives 'error: unknown command "check"' (exit 2), and `alerts` itself is missing from the table.
defects.detection_hint: Compare the README command list with COMMANDS in src/cli.ts or `node dist/cli.js --help`.

defects.description: '// TODO: honour opts.quietHours': the quietHours option is declared (engine.ts 33-34), validated in the config schema (schema.ts 119-121) and passed by the CLI (cli.ts 305), but never used, so users who configure quiet hours still get notified during them.
defects.detection_hint: TODO in the constructor; opts.quietHours is never read. Needs an owner decision: implement, or reject/warn on the setting instead of silently accepting it.

defects.description: The test 'dispatches fired alerts to every notifier' only asserts expect(result).toBeTruthy(); the recorded `seen` events and result.fired/delivered are never checked, so it passes even if dispatch is broken.
defects.detection_hint: Test name promises a behaviour its only assertion cannot detect; mutating dispatch() leaves it green.

defects.description: A placeholder API key literal is committed and used as the fallback for PRICEWATCH_BINANCE_API_KEY (line 36), so every request sends X-MBX-APIKEY with a fake key (line 43). Real Binance rejects an invalid key even on public endpoints, which turns every ticker into a failure (and, via D09, a 0 valuation). Credentials must come only from configuration.
defects.detection_hint: String literal matching sk_test_* assigned to DEFAULT_API_KEY; secret scanners flag it. Fix = drop the default and send the header only when a key is configured.

defects.description: Cooldown timestamps are saved with toLocaleString() and read back with new Date(string). The format depends on the machine locale and drops the timezone: under fr-FR, 5 Sept 2026 12:00 is written as '05/09/2026 12:00:00' and read back as 9 May; '23/09/2026 ...' reads as Invalid Date (NaN), so the cooldown never applies and every run re-notifies.
defects.detection_hint: toLocaleString() used for persistence; Date parsing of a non-ISO string. Fix = store ISO 8601 UTC or epoch ms.

defects.description: The value table is sorted by the formatted money string of the VALUE column, lexicographically: '30,000.00 USDT' sorts above '120,000.00 USDT', contradicting 'largest position first'. The comparator never returns 0 either.
defects.detection_hint: String '<' comparison on display strings inside rows.sort(); sort the holdings by numeric value before formatting.

traps.description: File notifier plugin that no module imports statically (neither do console.ts and webhook.ts next to it). Dead-file tools report it as unused.
traps.why_required: Plugins are loaded by the name given in the config: loadNotifier() builds `builtin/${name}${ext}` and imports it at runtime (src/plugins/loader.ts 47-50). examples/config.example.json and the README use { "plugin": "file" }; deleting it breaks `pricewatch alerts` and the `plugins` listing.
traps.hidden_test: tests/plugins.test.ts ('"file" appends one JSON line per alert', 'lists every built-in plugin'); tests/cli-behaviour.test.ts ('notifies through the plugins named in the config')

traps.description: Bare side-effect import `import './exchange/adapters/index.js';` with no bindings; looks like an unused import.
traps.why_required: Evaluating the adapter modules is what calls registerExchange('binance'|'kraken'). Without it createExchange() from the package entry point (and the CLI, which goes through src/index.ts) fails with 'unknown exchange'.
traps.hidden_test: tests/exchange-registry.test.ts (imports only src/index.ts); every CLI test in tests/cli-behaviour.test.ts and tests/snapshot-contract.test.ts

traps.description: Kraken adapter: KrakenClient is exported but never imported by name anywhere, and no visible test covers it.
traps.why_required: It is reached only through registry resolution by string: registerExchange('kraken', ...) at line 63, loaded by the side-effect import in adapters/index.ts line 5, selected by "exchange": "kraken" in the config or `--exchange kraken`. README lists kraken as supported and uses it in the library example.
traps.hidden_test: tests/exchange-registry.test.ts ('resolves "kraken" by name and parses its ticker payload'); tests/cli-behaviour.test.ts ('uses the kraken adapter when the exchange is overridden')

traps.description: splitPair() has no caller inside src/ or the visible tests; only src/index.ts line 42 re-exports it.
traps.why_required: It is public library API documented in README 'Library usage' (splitPair('xbt/usd')); src/index.ts is the package entry point, so external consumers import it.
traps.hidden_test: tests/public-api.test.ts ('exports splitPair', 'splitPair splits and normalizes both legs', 'splitPair rejects strings that are not BASE/QUOTE')

traps.description: Missing market for a pegged stablecoin falls back to price 1: looks like the same success-shaped fallback as D09 on the next line.
traps.why_required: Intentional and documented (README 'Pegged assets', DEFAULT_PEGGED, `"pegged": []` to opt out); the fallback is visible through priceSource 'peg' and the '*' marker in the table. Removing it values USDC/DAI balances at 0 or makes valuation fail on venues without stablecoin pairs.

traps.description: schemaVersion is written into every snapshot (field declared at line 22, constant at lines 3-8) but never read anywhere in the code base.
traps.why_required: It is part of the JSON output contract of `pricewatch snapshot` documented in README 'JSON snapshot format'; downstream consumers key their parsers on it.
traps.hidden_test: tests/snapshot-contract.test.ts (all cases); tests/public-api.test.ts ('exposes the snapshot schema version and error classes')

traps.description: `default:` branch of the switch over rule.kind, assigning the rule to `never`: the type checker considers it unreachable and config validation already rejects unknown kinds.
traps.why_required: Rules also arrive through the library API from untyped JSON (evaluateRule, AlertEngine are public). The branch makes an unknown or newly-added kind throw UnsupportedRuleError instead of silently never firing, and the `never` assignment makes the compiler flag a new union member without an evaluator.

traps.description: getTickers() awaits each request inside a for loop (a classic 'use Promise.all' target) and catches per-asset failures with only a warn log (looks like a swallowed error).
traps.why_required: Sequential on purpose: the public endpoints are weight-limited per IP and the MinIntervalLimiter spaces calls; the commit 'fix(exchange): fetch tickers sequentially...' records the HTTP 429s the parallel version caused. Skipping failed assets is the documented ExchangeClient contract (lines 23-26) that the peg fallback (X05) depends on; missing-price handling belongs in valuation (D09).
